title: Dynamic motion aftereffect matched by real motion (Hiris & Blake, 1992)
summary: How much downward motion does upward-motion adaptation add to random dots? Compare two dot displays after adaptation, then without it. The shift in their matching point measures the dynamic motion aftereffect in percentage signal. An adaptation of Hiris & Blake’s two-display procedure.
references: Hiris, E., & Blake, R. (1992). Another perspective on the visual motion aftereffect. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA, 89(19), 9025-9028. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.89.19.9025
Williams, D. W., & Sekuler, R. (1984). Coherent global motion percepts from stochastic local motions. Vision Research, 24(1), 55-62. (the RDVN convention the paper cites)

deviations.original: Apple 12-inch monochrome monitor, P4 phosphor, 640 x 480, 67 Hz, Macintosh II (p. 9025)
deviations.here: Any calibrated display; dots step every whole number of frames, e.g. 3 frames (50 ms) at 60 Hz, so the speed is 1.91 deg/s rather than the paper's ~2 deg/s (about 2.1 deg/s if it stepped every third 67-Hz frame)
deviations.reason: A modern display; the step size and speed are the paper's, rounded to this display's frames

deviations.here: Full white (signed RGB 1) on whatever luminance the display gives; background_cd_m2 records the paper's value but nothing sets it
deviations.reason: alhazen does not control luminance; set the display with a photometer before a real session

deviations.here: 2 arcmin rounded to the rig's pixels (2.4 px on the example booth at 114 cm), at least 1 px
deviations.reason: Pixel size depends on the rig; at short viewing distances the dots become a single pixel

deviations.original: The authors EH and RB in Fig. 1 (p. 9026); "a number of people" for the informal matches
deviations.here: Any adult observer, naive or not

tasks.title: Coherence matching after motion adaptation (Fig. 1)
tasks.summary: Adapted set (paper Fig. 1, experimental curve). Adaptation (60 s, then 10 s before every test): the left display's 100 dots all move upward, the right display shows random dynamic visual noise. Test, 2 s: the left display has a variable percentage of dots moving downward (or upward) among random dots, the right display 40 % downward. The observer presses the arrow for the display that looked more coherently downward.

parameters.name: adapt_mode
parameters.label: Adaptation
parameters.meaning: unidirectional: the adapted display's dots all move in the adapting direction while the other display shows RDVN (the paper's experimental curve). random: both show RDVN (the control set).

parameters.name: adapt_direction_deg
parameters.label: Adapting direction
parameters.meaning: Direction of the adapting motion, degrees counter-clockwise from rightward (90 = upward). The aftereffect, and + test signal, go the opposite way.

parameters.name: adapted_side
parameters.label: Adapted display
parameters.meaning: Which display adapts to the motion and carries the variable test signal; the other shows RDVN during adaptation and the fixed reference in the test.

parameters.name: test_levels_pct
parameters.label: Test signal levels
parameters.meaning: Signed percentage of signal dots in the adapted display's test: + move opposite the adaptation (downward), - with it (upward). One cell per level. ASSUMED set: the paper's Fig. 1 axis spans -20 to 60 % without listing the levels.

parameters.name: reference_signal_pct
parameters.label: Reference signal
parameters.meaning: Percentage of signal dots moving downward in the other display's test, fixed.

parameters.name: n_dots
parameters.label: Dots per display
parameters.meaning: Black dots in each circular display, in every phase.

parameters.name: dot_size_dva
parameters.label: Dot size
parameters.meaning: Side of each square dot (the paper: 2 arcmin; 2 x 2 pixels). At least one pixel is drawn.

parameters.name: aperture_dva
parameters.label: Display diameter
parameters.meaning: Diameter of each circular dot display.

parameters.name: aperture_gap_dva
parameters.label: Gap between displays
parameters.meaning: Distance between the nearest edges of the two displays; the fixation cross is midway.

parameters.name: speed_dva_s
parameters.label: Dot speed
parameters.meaning: Speed of every dot, signal or noise (the paper: ~2 deg/s). With the step size it sets how many frames pass between steps.

parameters.name: step_dva
parameters.label: Step size
parameters.meaning: Distance a dot jumps at each step: the paper's 5 pixels converted with an ASSUMED pixel size of its 12-inch 640 x 480 monitor at 114 cm. Dots step every round(step / speed x refresh) frames (3 at 60 Hz, about 1.91 deg/s).

parameters.name: dot_color
parameters.label: Dot colour
parameters.meaning: Signed RGB of the dots: black.

parameters.name: background_rgb
parameters.label: Background
parameters.meaning: Signed RGB of the whole screen: white.

parameters.name: background_cd_m2
parameters.label: Background luminance
parameters.meaning: The paper's white was 15 cd/m2. Documentation only: set the display with a photometer; the task does not control luminance.

parameters.name: fix_size_dva
parameters.label: Fixation cross size
parameters.meaning: Arm length of the black cross midway between the displays. ASSUMED.

parameters.name: initial_adaptation
parameters.label: Initial adaptation
parameters.meaning: Adaptation before the first test of a session (and after a long pause).

parameters.name: topup_adaptation
parameters.label: Top-up adaptation
parameters.meaning: Adaptation displays shown again before every other test, to keep the adaptation up.

parameters.name: test_duration
parameters.label: Test duration
parameters.meaning: How long the two test displays are shown.

parameters.name: response_timeout
parameters.label: Response window
parameters.meaning: After the test, how long a key is accepted; without one the level is served again. ASSUMED.

parameters.name: readapt_after
parameters.label: Re-adapt after a pause
parameters.meaning: A pause longer than this since the last test display brings back the initial adaptation. ASSUMED; the paper describes no pauses.

parameters.name: key_left
parameters.label: Key for the left display
parameters.meaning: The left display looked more coherently downward. ASSUMED.

parameters.name: key_right
parameters.label: Key for the right display
parameters.meaning: The right display looked more coherently downward. ASSUMED.

parameters.name: paradigm.n_per_condition
parameters.label: Judgments per level
parameters.meaning: Trials per test level; the paper's points were 20 judgments each.

outcomes.name: CHOSE_TEST
outcomes.meaning: The adapted (variable) display was judged more coherently downward.

outcomes.name: CHOSE_REFERENCE
outcomes.meaning: The 40 % reference display was judged more coherently downward.

outcomes.name: NO_RESPONSE
outcomes.meaning: No key within the response window; the level is served again.

events.name: ADAPT_ON
events.meaning: First frame of the adaptation (initial or top-up) displays.

events.name: TEST_ON
events.meaning: First frame of the two test displays.

events.name: RESPONSE_CUE
events.meaning: Test displays off, cross alone: the answer is accepted from this flip; reaction time runs from it.
